target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## What Problem This Solves

macOS LaunchAgent regeneration could erase an active channel credential from the generated service-env file when the update/restart shell did not re-export that config SecretRef. The next gateway process then started without the token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service install plan now receives the installed environment-value provenance and can retain an existing value only when all of these remain true:

- current config still references the normalized key as a SecretRef;
- the key is a safe service environment name;
- the installed value came from OpenClaw's generated file (`file` or `inline-and-file`).

The retained value is fallback-only: current state-dir dotenv, shell, and auth sources still win. Start-time stale-service repair forwards the same provenance into this one canonical plan.

Deep review found and fixed an important boundary bug in the earlier patch: filtering against all managed keys could resurrect a stale generated-file value after config moved the key to `env.vars`. The final code filters strictly against current config SecretRef keys. Retired refs, source migrations, unsafe keys, and inline-only values are dropped.

## User Impact

Gateway reinstall/update/restart no longer wipes active generated-file-backed SecretRef credentials merely because the invoking shell lacks them. Credential rotation and explicit current sources remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 49 focused tests passed (48 install-plan cases and one start-repair case).
- Regression coverage includes two active SecretRefs, retired managed keys, `env.vars` source migration, unsafe names, provenance filtering, and source precedence.
- Blacksmith Testbox: remote formatting passed for all touched files.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview: clean, confidence 0.93.
- Native review artifacts: validated, zero findings.
- Contributor live macOS proof: secret-absent LaunchAgent regeneration kept a 0600 service-env file and token equality; `launchctl` reported the temporary service active; Telegram `getMe` succeeded with the regenerated-file token; cleanup completed.

The live macOS proof was captured on the contributor pre-sync head. The current exact tree is verified by patch-continuity review plus the focused Testbox regressions above.

## What Problem This Solves

When two autonomous agent turns are adjacent in Control UI history, a successful reply in the later turn could make a failed tool from the earlier turn render as `Tool output` instead of `Tool error`.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(infra): include update timeout in managed-service handoff parent exit wait
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99666. Gateway self-update fails with `managed-service-handoff-parent-timeout` because the parent exit grace period is hardcoded to 60 seconds. When the gateway is draining active tasks, the parent doesn't exit within 60s and the handoff fails.

## Root Cause / Fix

`startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff` computed `parentExitTimeoutMs` as `restartDelayMs + 60_000` regardless of the update timeout. The caller already passes `timeoutMs` but it was not used.

**Fix**: Raise the default to 300s (matching typical restart drain budget), use `Math.max(300_000, timeoutMs ?? 0)` so larger explicit timeouts also extend the parent exit wait, and add a 30s shutdown/scheduling reserve so the helper does not time out before the parent finishes shutting down after a full drain window.

Changes (2 files, +18/-2):
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts`: 2 lines changed + 30s reserve constant
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts`: 2 tests updated for new reserve

## Evidence

### Production Function Proof
```
$ node --import tsx proof.ts
Proof: parentExitTimeoutMs includes 30 s shutdown reserve

  PASS default (no timeoutMs) = 330000
  PASS 5min timeout = 330000
  PASS small timeout (floor at 300s + reserve) = 330000
  PASS 30min + 500ms restart = 1830500

ALL CHECKS PASSED

target.title: fix(voice-call): deliver early TTS via onEarlyText before compaction wait
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice-call callers hear silence until post-turn compaction completes because `generateVoiceResponse()` waits for the full `runEmbeddedAgent()` promise before extracting text and calling `manager.speak()`. This PR uses the existing `blockReplyBreak`/`onBlockReply` contract to deliver spoken text to TTS as soon as the first block reply arrives.

Additionally fixes an async fallback race: `onEarlyText` was fire-and-forget — the `.then()` that sets `earlyTextSpoken = true` runs in a microtask that may not be settled when `generateVoiceResponse` reads the flag after `runEmbeddedAgent` resolves. If the TTS I/O (real network call) takes longer than the agent run, `earlyTextSpoken` stays `false` and the webhook fires a duplicate fallback `speak()`.

Fixes #79521

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`response-generator.ts`**: Adds `onEarlyText?: (text: string) => Promise<boolean>` to `VoiceResponseParams`. In the `onBlockReply` handler, extracts spoken text from the first block reply, fires `onEarlyText` immediately, and **stores the returned promise**. Before returning from `generateVoiceResponse`, **awaits the pending promise** so the fallback-speak decision always sees the settled TTS outcome. The callback must return `true` for confirmed TTS delivery; `earlyTextSpoken` is gated on this return value so a failed early speak does not suppress the final fallback.
- **`webhook.ts`**: Passes `onEarlyText` that calls `this.manager.speak(callId, text)` and returns `speakResult.success`. Falls back to the post-run speak only when `earlyTextSpoken` is false (no block reply arrived, early delivery failed, or early delivery threw).
- **`response-generator.test.ts`**: 19 tests. Covers: `onEarlyText` fires before a deferred `runEmbeddedAgent` settles; TTS resolve-after-run race (`await pendingEarlyText`); fallback when no block reply arrives; fallback when `onEarlyText` returns `false`; fallback when `onEarlyText` throws.

## User Impact

Voice-call users hear TTS speech as soon as the agent produces its first block reply, instead of waiting for the full post-turn compaction cycle. Failed early delivery safely falls back to the existing post-run speak path. The duplicate-speak race (successful early TTS followed by a fallback speak of the same text) is eliminated.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts` — 19/19 passed
- `oxlint --quiet` on changed files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on changed files — clean

Behavior addressed: Early TTS delivery via `onBlockReply` callback with confirmed-delivery gate for fallback safety, and `await pendingEarlyText` to close the async race window between TTS resolution and the fallback-speak decision.

Real environment tested: Linux (Node 24), branch `fix/issue-79521-voice-call-block-reply`, commit `8bae4072`

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts --run
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.ts extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.ts extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
   Duration  10.46s

$ oxlint — no errors in changed files
$ oxfmt — all matched files use the correct format
```

Observed result after fix: `onEarlyText` fires from within `onBlockReply` before `runEmbeddedAgent` resolves. The returned promise is stored in `pendingEarlyText` and awaited before `generateVoiceResponse` returns. When TTS resolves after the agent run (the real-world race), `earlyTextSpoken` correctly reflects `true` and the webhook fallback speak is suppressed. When `onEarlyText` returns `false` or throws, `earlyTextSpoken` stays `undefined` and the final post-run fallback speak still fires. When no block reply arrives, the existing fallback to `result.payloads` works as before.

Review feedback addressed:
- ClawSweeper P1 finding — `earlyTextSpoken` is gated on confirmed `onEarlyText` delivery success rather than callback invocation, preserving the fallback speak path when early playback fails.
- ClawSweeper P2 finding (this revision) — `pendingEarlyText` is awaited before the fallback-speak decision, closing the async race where successful TTS could be followed by a duplicate fallback speak.

What was not tested: No live Twilio/VoIP roundtrip was performed. The `onEarlyText`→`manager.speak()` path is unit-tested at the `response-generator` level but not through a real WebSocket/STT/TTS pipeline.

- token endpoint failures expose the raw Open Platform JSON without telling the user which OpenClaw settings to fix;
- API/network errors include the low-level failure but no setup path.

## Changes

- Add a small shared QQBot setup-guidance helper that points users to `QQBOT_APP_ID`, `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the QQBot setup docs.
- Use that guidance for missing gateway/outbound credentials.
- Append the guidance to token endpoint failures when `access_token` is absent.
- Append the guidance to structured QQBot API errors and network errors.
- Add regression tests for token, structured API, and network error messages.

## Testing

target.title: feat(release): add extended-stable npm closeout
target.body:
Closes #100504

## What Problem This Solves

Extended-stable publication already publishes and verifies every npm-publishable official plugin before direct OIDC core publication, but it has no safe way to freeze final registry state after publication. If package bytes publish and registry readback alone fails, rerunning the publish workflow risks colliding with an immutable npm version. The release also lacks durable proof that `latest` stayed unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a separate five-input closeout workflow with read-only repository and Actions permissions and no npm credential, OIDC publish permission, or release environment. It authenticates the exact preflight, plugin, Full Release Validation, and core runs; accepts only a tightly bounded publish-success/readback-only failed core run; verifies `openclaw`, `@openclaw/ai`, every canonical `all-publishable` plugin, and the preserved later-month `latest`; then uploads one deterministic compact registry snapshot.

The existing plugin-first/core-last OIDC publication path is unchanged. Candidate tags, cross-repository promotion, rollback/cleanup protocols, and all non-npm release surfaces remain out of scope. Automated selector repair remains deferred; the workflow prints both applicable credential-isolated core repair commands and can be rerun without publication authority.

## User Impact

Release operators can close out a normal extended-stable publish or recover after an ambiguous registry readback without republishing immutable bytes. Existing `stable` continues to resolve npm `latest`; `extended-stable` remains an additive npm-only channel.

## Evidence

- Focused Vitest: 6 files, 119 tests passed.
- Workflow YAML parsing and Node syntax checks passed for plugin, core, and closeout surfaces.
- [Inspectable isolated Verdaccio proof](https://gist.github.com/kevinslin/88a03a634a316eaf077a6b46424b1730) passed new `.33`, patch `.34`, stale-selector rejection, repaired `.35` convergence, and unchanged `latest`.
- Static workflow contract scans plugin, core, and closeout execution surfaces and rejects GitHub Release, Docker, desktop, website, mobile, ClawHub, and broad-orchestrator dispatch.
- Independent correctness, documentation, and dead-code reviews were completed; all accepted blocker/major findings were fixed and reverified.
- Companion evidence change: https://github.com/kevinslin/releases/pull/1. The upstream `openclaw/releases` target rejects PR creation for the available personal, work, and connected-App credentials; the fork PR is a takeover-ready review artifact for commit `cb5d832bac1568ab0865fca36300563e352fe846`.
- Local Testbox execution was unavailable because the installed Crabbox is `0.16.0` while the Blacksmith provider requires `0.22.0+`; current-head CI is the broad hosted verification gate.

## AI Assistance

- [x] AI-assisted implementation and review.
- [x] I understand the workflow, registry, and evidence changes.

target.title: fix: let Ollama incomplete streams use model fallback
target.body:
Closes #100460

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Ollama as the primary model provider would receive a terminal `LLM request failed` instead of moving to a configured fallback model when Ollama ended a stream with `Ollama API stream ended without a final response`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama stream reader already raises a precise provider-runtime error for this incomplete-stream case. This change classifies that exact Ollama signal as a timeout-style failover reason and lets the embedded-result fallback path continue for the same exact payload, including custom Ollama provider ids that follow the documented `ollama-*` convention such as `ollama-5080`.

The change deliberately keeps generic timeout-like embedded error payloads non-retryable, so arbitrary provider error text does not become fallback-worthy.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Ollama users with `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` configured can recover from this transient incomplete-stream failure by moving to the next model candidate instead of getting a dead-end channel error.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts`
  - 2 Vitest shards passed
  - 260 tests passed
- `git diff --check`
- Local Ollama smoke with `smollm2:135m` returned HTTP 200 and a final streamed chunk with `done: true`.
- Targeted runtime probe after the fix:
  - `ollama` exact incomplete-stream message -> `timeout`
  - `ollama-remote` exact incomplete-stream message -> `timeout`
  - `openai` plus the same message -> `null`

Proof gaps:

- Remote Crabbox/Testbox proof was not available from this machine: Blacksmith CLI was missing and AWS Crabbox broker login was not configured.
- The live Ollama smoke proves the local stream path is usable; it does not force Ollama to naturally truncate a stream before `done: true`.

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper now treats Mantis web UI chat proof as a supported proof lane in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/424, but OpenClaw did not yet have a focused Mantis workflow that can run and publish that proof. ## Why This Change Was Made

The intended scope is deliberately narrow: OpenClaw web UI chat transcript and chat interaction proof only. This does not make Mantis a general browser, WinUI, dashboard, settings-page, or arbitrary visual proof worker. Those surfaces should still use ordinary Playwright/browser proof, maintainer screenshots/manual proof, Crabbox where appropriate, or normal local artifacts.

## User Impact

Maintainers get a dedicated web UI chat proof lane that can validate a candidate ref, run a focused Control UI chat E2E proof, produce screenshot/video/metadata artifacts, and publish Mantis evidence for PR review. Contributors do not get a new product-facing UI feature.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress typing for unmentioned group runs regardless of delivery mode
target.body:
## Summary

**What problem does this PR solve?**

On silent agent runs, `signalTextDelta` fires `sendPresenceUpdate("composing")` if the model streams renderable text before the silent-token decision. Once fired, composing is never retracted. Group members see a persistent "typing..." indicator on every background run that ends silently.

The previous fix (commit `5152d8beb4`, `fix(whatsapp): suppress silent-run typing indicators`) added `suppressTyping` with this condition:

```
suppressTyping: sourceRepliesAreToolOnly && chatType === "group" && !wasMentioned
```

`sourceRepliesAreToolOnly` derives from the _configured_ delivery mode (`message_tool_only`). It is not a runtime prediction of whether the current run will produce visible output. Groups configured with `automatic` delivery — the most common case — are entirely excluded by this gate, and those are exactly the groups where silent background runs happen most often.

This PR replaces it with the correct boundary:

```
// Before (5152d8beb4)
suppressTyping: sourceRepliesAreToolOnly && chatType === "group" && !wasMentioned

// After
suppressTyping: chatType === "group" && !wasMentioned && !sourceReplyCommandAuthorized
```

**Why this is the right gate**

The correct question is not "what delivery mode is this group configured for?" It is "was the bot explicitly addressed?" If `wasMentioned` is false and no owner command was invoked, the run is passive. Passive runs can end silently regardless of delivery mode. Composing should not fire for them.

`!sourceReplyCommandAuthorized` carves out owner slash commands (`/status`, `/new`). Those are explicitly directed at the bot and will produce a visible reply — they should keep their typing indicator. This carve-out also satisfies the pre-existing test `"delivers authorized WhatsApp group text slash command replies visibly"` (line 1050 of `inbound-dispatch.test.ts`), which asserts `suppressTyping: false` for authorized commands. Removing `sourceRepliesAreToolOnly` without this carve-out would break that test.

The reason `5152d8beb4` kept `sourceRepliesAreToolOnly`: at the time, the command test had no `suppressTyping` assertion, so the broad `!wasMentioned` condition from an earlier draft was narrowed back to avoid breaking it when the assertion was added. `sourceRepliesAreToolOnly` was the smallest safe gate. This PR replaces it with the semantically correct one.

**What is the intended outcome?**

All passive unmentioned group runs — any delivery mode — produce no composing indicator. @mention runs, direct-chat runs, and authorized commands are unaffected.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

A structural fix. Fully preventing false composing when the model streams pre-silence text requires collapsing the eager streaming tap and the lazy delivery decision into a single pipeline. `suppressTyping` is the pragmatic mitigation.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

Whether `!sourceReplyCommandAuthorized` covers all explicitly-invoked group paths that should retain composing, or whether any are missing. The tradeoff — rare proactive visible replies in unmentioned groups arrive without a typing flash — is intentional and documented in the comment.

---

## Linked context

Closes #

Related to the investigation documented in #88642.

Self-identified from live session logs.

---

## Current reproducibility

The symptom was observed on 2026-05-27 with OpenClaw `2026.5.24` against a `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` checkpoint that Google has since updated server-side without changing the model ID. That checkpoint emitted `<think>…</think>` XML as a plain text part (no `thought: true` flag) — which `isRenderableText` passes — before `<final>NO_REPLY</final>`, triggering composing. The current checkpoint does not reproduce the symptom; the exact internal change is not known, but the most likely explanation is that reasoning is now routed through `thought: true` parts rather than plain text.

The fix is justified independently of current reproducibility: `sourceRepliesAreToolOnly` is structurally the wrong gate for the reasons above, and any model that emits pre-silence text in a future checkpoint will re-trigger it.

---

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Spurious WhatsApp "typing..." on silent agent runs in unmentioned groups.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, OpenClaw `2026.5.31`, `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, WhatsApp group, `requireMention: false`, system prompt instructs silent web search with no reply.
- **Exact steps run after this patch:** Three messages to the group — no @mention (silent), @mention (visible reply), no @mention (silent).
- **Evidence after fix (2026-06-01):**

```
# Run 1 — no mention, silent
15:34:09  embedded run start
15:34:25  embedded run tool start: tool=web_search
15:34:43  Skipping auto-reply: silent token or no text/media returned from resolver
          ← zero [TYPING] sendComposing entries ✓

# Run 2 — @mention, replied
15:34:57  embedded run start
15:34:59  embedded run tool start: tool=web_search
15:35:04  Skipping recent outbound WhatsApp echo 3EB00C…  ← message sent ✓

# Run 3 — no mention, silent
15:35:21  embedded run start
15:35:27  embedded run tool start: tool=web_search
15:35:34  Skipping auto-reply: silent token
          ← zero [TYPING] sendComposing entries ✓
```

- **Observed result:** No composing on silent unmentioned runs; normal typing indicator on @mention run.
- **Before evidence:** Historical only. Session file entry `2026-05-27T15:05:58.321Z`: `TEXT block[1]` (no `thought: true`) is `'<think>The system prompt dictates…</think><final>NO_REPLY</final>'`. `isRenderableText("<think>") = true`. Log shows `[TYPING] sendComposing → 120363406415684625@g.us` followed by `Skipping auto-reply: silent token`.
- **What was not tested:** Live before-state (model behavior changed — see above). Other channels (change is WhatsApp-only).
- **Proof limitations:** Cannot demonstrate Cause 2 before/after live today. The after-fix proof demonstrates correct composing behavior across the three affected scenarios.

---

## Tests and validation

```
pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch
pnpm test extensions/whatsapp
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json
```

All pass.

**What regression coverage was added or updated?**

`inbound-dispatch.test.ts`: the test `"honors automatic visible replies for WhatsApp groups"` previously asserted `suppressTyping: false` for an unmentioned `automatic`-delivery group run — asserting the wrong behavior. Updated to `suppressTyping: true` and renamed to `"suppresses typing for automatic-delivery unmentioned group chat"`. All other `suppressTyping` assertions (mentioned group, direct chat, authorized command) pass unchanged.

**What failed before this fix?**

The `sourceRepliesAreToolOnly` gate left all `automatic`-delivery groups exposed to spurious composing. Observed with the Gemini checkpoint described above on 2026-05-27.

---

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — WhatsApp group members no longer see a typing indicator on silent unmentioned runs. On rare proactive visible replies in unmentioned groups, the typing flash is also absent (intentional tradeoff).

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No.

**What is the highest-risk area?**

Proactive visible replies in unmentioned groups arrive without a preceding typing flash. This is accepted: false indicators on every silent background run erode trust; a missing flash on a rare proactive reply is a minor UX gap.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

Authorized commands and @mention runs retain their typing indicator. Direct-chat runs are unaffected.

---

## Current review state

Ready for review.

target.body:
Fixes #95279

## 2026-07-05 round-2 CI refresh

- Attributed the two failed checks from the prior update. `checks-node-compact-large-3` was a current-PR expectation miss in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`: room-event transcript recorder messages now intentionally expose the trusted inbound fields added by this PR, so the regression expectation includes `inboundDecorated: true` / `bareBody` alongside the existing `__openclaw.senderIsOwner` metadata.
- `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` was stale-main drift rather than trusted-inbound logic: the branch was missing current-main's `src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` expected-route update for `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-mcp-real-transports.test.ts` importing `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts`. A fresh `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` reported `sync_main_required=true`; `daily_fix.sh sync-main` replayed the PR onto current main, then a follow-up drift check reported `sync_main_required=false` for the next main commit.
- Round-2 local head is `6f35823170cb455a2d5e845d77b5836ee1f55f5f`. Fresh validation from the round-2 tree passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `CI=1 pnpm exec vitest run src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --reporter=verbose`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-20260705-round2-core.tsbuildinfo`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-20260705-round2-core-test.tsbuildinfo`, and `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8` all exited 0.
- External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment, so this update continues to rely on local transcript/UI/CLI/runtime regression proof and keeps that gap disclosed below.

## 2026-07-05 conflict refresh

- Replayed the branch onto current `origin/main` with `daily_fix.sh sync-main` after `check-main-drift` reported `sync_main_required=true` for merge conflicts / overlapping related files. The replay completed with no unresolved conflict markers; the synced head is `3dd723e724f9049bdbb5cdfcf795b89b6ba7182d`.
- Conflict resolution preserves both current-main ownership metadata (`senderIsOwner` stored under `__openclaw`) and this PR's trusted inbound-decoration contract (`inboundDecorated` / `bareBody`). The `before_message_write` redaction boundary still drops trusted inbound fields when hook output rewrites `content`, while preserving safe metadata such as `idempotencyKey` and `senderIsOwner`.
- The current-main UI chat files now live under `ui/src/lib/chat/...`; the synced diff preserves this PR's trusted bare-body extraction/normalization coverage on that layout.
- A follow-up `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` saw a newer `origin/main` `0720b322fedd97c7a37727bdb6e73fcd9c43fab7`, but reported `has_conflicts=false`, `sync_main_required=false`, and no overlap files, so no second sync was required.
- Fresh validation from the synced head passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-20260705-core.tsbuildinfo`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-20260705-core-test.tsbuildinfo`, and `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8` all exited 0.
- External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment, so this update continues to rely on local transcript/UI/CLI/runtime regression proof and keeps that gap disclosed below.

## 2026-06-28 rescue update

- Rebased the contributor branch onto current `origin/main` (`830467bc93`) and resolved the only manual conflict in `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.ts`, preserving both main's `isTextContentBlockType(...)` support and this PR's trusted bare-body extraction path.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 redaction-boundary blocker: `preparePersistedUserTurnMessageForTranscriptWrite(...)` now drops `inboundDecorated` / `bareBody` whenever a `before_message_write` hook rewrites user `content`, including spread-style redaction hooks. Added a regression test covering `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }`.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 type blocker: `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` now accepts any message-like object (`object | null | undefined`) and defensively reads the runtime-attached trusted fields, which removes the `TS2559` failures at the LLM-boundary and CLI imported-history call sites without requiring unsafe call-site casts. (An earlier attempt used a generic `<T extends object>`; that tripped `no-unnecessary-type-parameters` in `check-lint`, so the parameter is a plain `object`.)
- Kept memory-host session-file tests stable on Windows by asserting classification paths through the exported comparison normalizer and tolerating transient `EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY`/`EPERM` fixture cleanup during teardown. No cross-package import is added, so the memory-host-sdk private-package contract surface is unchanged (the `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-b` boundary check passes).
- Resolved the merge conflict: PR head is now `MERGEABLE` against `main`.

Additional verification after the rebase/repair:

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts
# Test Files 1 passed; Tests 28 passed; exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts
# Test Files 5 passed; Tests 145 passed; exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
# Test Files 3 passed; Tests 83 passed; exit=0

git diff --check
# exit=0
```

Local note: direct extension type-check targets were also attempted, but the local shared `node_modules` symlink is missing unrelated extension dependencies/exports (`@openclaw/crabline`, `acpx/runtime` members) in files outside this PR's diff; core production/test type-check targets for the touched code pass as shown above.

## Summary

- **What did NOT change:** This does not remove legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not change active-turn model prompt construction, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type literal metadata-looking text should not lose that text from the control UI, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory session corpus, or model historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- Behavior or issue addressed: user-authored text that looks like OpenClaw inbound metadata could be stripped or deduped incorrectly because consumers parsed forgeable sentinel text from `content`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, a local `pnpm exec tsx` proof harness that persisted a real transcript row with `appendUserTurnTranscriptMessage(...)` then ran Control UI `normalizeMessage(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` against that row, and a CLI imported-session dedupe proof harness that called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two distinct trusted `bareBody` values sharing the same decorated model-facing `content`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The targeted regression tests completed successfully with no test failures, `git diff --check` completed with no whitespace errors, the live transcript proof showed the persisted decorated row rendering/extracting the trusted bare body while preserving literal `Sender (untrusted metadata):` user text, and the CLI dedupe proof preserved two distinct trusted bare bodies instead of collapsing them by identical decorated content.
- **What was not tested:** SonarLint was unavailable in this environment (`sonarlint: command not found`); `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a crabbox launcher sanity-check failure; full `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false --incremental false` hit Node heap out-of-memory even with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`; an external live gateway/channel proof was unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment, so the proof here is local transcript/UI/CLI behavior using repository runtime code and synthetic data only.
- Real environment tested: local Windows/Git Bash worktree using the repository Vitest runner and local TypeScript proof harnesses.
- Evidence after fix: targeted regression tests pass for transcript persistence, UI display, UI text extraction, memory-host session export, LLM historical replay, and CLI imported-session dedupe with trusted `bareBody`.

Transcript/UI proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-live-proof-harness> <scratch-output-dir>

Real transcript row with trusted bare body:
{
  "role": "user",
  "contentPreview": "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"message_id\":\"msg-live-proof\"}\n",
  "inboundDecorated": true,
  "bareBody": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event"
}

Control UI render/extraction result from the persisted row:
{
  "normalizedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "extractedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "preservedLiteralSenderSentinel": true,
  "usedTrustedBareBodyInsteadOfDecoratedCopy": true,
  "systemMarkersNeutralized": true
}

before_message_write redaction boundary:
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "[redacted by hook]",
  "idempotencyKey": "live-proof:redaction",
  "hasBareBody": false,
  "hasInboundDecorated": false
}

Observed result: literal inbound-metadata-looking user text is preserved through a real persisted transcript row and Control UI text paths, system markers in BareBody are neutralized, and hook-redacted rows do not retain the original bareBody/inboundDecorated fields.
```

CLI imported-session dedupe proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-cli-dedupe-proof-harness>

{
  "mergedCount": 2,
  "preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies": true,
  "wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent": true,
  "bareBodies": [
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal first user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve first",
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal second user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve second"
  ]
}

Observed result: the CLI merge path kept both rows because trusted bare bodies differ, even though both rows had the same decorated model-facing content and would have collided if dedupe still used only forgeable sentinel-stripped content.
```

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`, `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Each consumer test covers a decorated inbound turn whose trusted bare body contains sentinel-shaped user text such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` plus fenced JSON; the expected behavior is that the trusted bare body is preserved literally instead of being parsed and stripped as metadata. The CLI imported-session test additionally proves two messages with identical decorated `content` but different trusted `bareBody` values do not dedupe into one row.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It locks the shared trusted-contract behavior at the persistence, UI, CLI dedupe, memory, and LLM replay boundaries without removing the legacy sentinel fallback or asserting unrelated prompt-construction details.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The parser/contract boundary was wrong: `buildInboundUserContextPrefix(...)` creates inbound metadata as plaintext blocks for model-facing prompts, and consumers such as UI history normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export, and LLM historical replay had no trusted way to distinguish host-added decoration from user-authored text in the same `content` channel.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The source-of-truth decision is no longer derived from forgeable `content` text. Consumers now use the shared trusted resolver and only accept `bareBody` when the message/context is explicitly marked `inboundDecorated: true` / `InboundDecorated: true`, so sentinel parsing remains only a legacy compatibility path.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for a public/data-format contract bug.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The change is additive, keeps legacy fallback behavior, and has targeted regression coverage for the affected consumer paths.
- **Patch quality notes:** Dynamic `as unknown` casts stay at existing message-union boundaries where `AgentMessage` can carry additive metadata; guard/default returns preserve existing fallback behavior; the multi-file diff follows the shared consumer contract boundary and is not a downstream masking workaround.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata (`inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody`, mirrored as `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody` on inbound context). Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers use that trusted contract when present and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## What Problem This Solves

Inbound context decoration is host-generated, but the decorated copy can live as text inside user-controlled user message content. Several consumers stripped or compared that decoration by matching forgeable sentinel strings such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` and fenced JSON. If a user typed the same shape intentionally, downstream display/history/dedupe/memory paths could drop real user text or collapse distinct imported messages.

This PR gives consumers a trusted, out-of-band contract for decorated inbound turns: a message/context marker that says the content may be decorated, plus the host-authored bare body to render/replay/index/dedupe.

## Source-of-truth boundary

The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata:

- runtime/persisted user messages: `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`
- inbound context: `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`

target.title: fix(control-ui): keep the dashboard mounted with a reconnect banner on gateway drops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Once the Control UI has an authenticated session, any WebSocket drop (gateway restart, laptop sleep, SSH-tunnel churn in the macOS app's remote mode, network blip) unmounts the entire dashboard and replaces it with the login gate showing a red "Could not connect" card — even though `GatewayBrowserClient` keeps auto-reconnecting with backoff underneath. The operator is visually "logged out" by a transient transport failure and loses all page context; when the retry succeeds the gate flashes back to the dashboard.

The disconnect-resilient machinery already existed but was unreachable: `chat-page.applyGatewaySnapshot` handles in-place disconnect/reconnect (queued sends marked "waiting for reconnect", history re-sync on reconnect) and the sidebar has an offline status dot — none of it ever visible because `OpenClawApp.render` swapped the shell for the gate the moment `connected` flipped false.

Fixes #100475.

## Why This Change Was Made

Failing gracefully requires distinguishing "transport interrupted, client is retrying" from "credentials rejected, operator input needed". That fact lives in the client's close handler, so it is now exported instead of re-derived:

- `ui/src/api/gateway.ts`: the close path computes `willRetry` once and uses it both to schedule the reconnect and to report it in `onClose` — a single source of truth for retry policy. Constructor failures (bad URL, mixed content) report `willRetry: false`.
- `ui/src/app/gateway-store.ts` (extracted from `bootstrap.ts` for a test seam, with an injectable client factory): the snapshot gains `reconnecting = everConnected && willRetry`, where `everConnected` tracks whether a hello succeeded this page lifetime. First-connect failures stay on the gate; established sessions degrade to reconnecting.
- `ui/src/app/app-host.ts`: the shell stays mounted while `reconnecting`, rendering an amber "Gateway connection lost — reconnecting…" banner (new `openclaw-connection-banner`) with a **Retry now** action. The login gate is reserved for first connects, credential rejections, and manual gate submissions (a `loginGatePinned` flag prevents shell flicker while a gate-submitted attempt is in flight).
- Event-gap recovery (`onGap` → fresh client) now also keeps the shell mounted instead of flashing the gate.
- `.callout.warn` CSS variant added — previously referenced by update status banners but never styled.

Keeping the shell mounted makes the existing per-page reconnect handling load-bearing (chat re-syncs subscriptions/queued sends on reconnect; the shell's `ensureAgentsList` already re-fetches on client change).

## User Impact

- Transient gateway drops no longer kick operators to the login form; the dashboard stays up with a status banner and recovers in place.
- Real credential problems (bad token/password, revoked pairing, rate limit) still land on the gate with the existing diagnostic cards.
- macOS app remote mode: a dead SSH tunnel now shows the dashboard + banner instead of a dead-end login form (the stale-tunnel-port endpoint refresh in the app is tracked separately in #100476).
- New i18n strings under `connection.*`, translated for all locales via `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` (0 fallbacks).
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md` gains a "Connection loss and reconnect" section.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts` (7 tests): first-connect failures stay on the gate; transport drop after hello → `reconnecting: true`; credential rejection → gate; event-gap recovery keeps `reconnecting`; `stop()` resets lineage; superseded clients cannot demote the snapshot.
- `ui/src/api/gateway.node.test.ts`: `willRetry` asserted on recoverable close, credential rejection (`AUTH_PASSWORD_MISMATCH`), both token-mismatch no-retry paths, and both constructor-failure paths.
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Blacksmith Testbox (run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28756286250).
- Local focused runs: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts ui/src/api/gateway.node.test.ts ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/proposals.test.ts` → green. (`ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.ts` fails identically on pristine HEAD in this macOS environment and is green on the Linux Testbox run above — pre-existing local flake, unrelated.)

target.title: feat(discord): add event-edit and event-delete actions
target.body:
## Summary - Problem: agents could create Discord scheduled events through the message tool but had no way to update or cancel them, so descriptions, locations, times, and cover art went stale until a human edited them in Discord - Why it matters: rounds out the scheduled-event lifecycle so agents (e.g. a Listening Party host swapping in a featured album) can keep event metadata in sync without human intervention - What changed: added `event-edit` and `event-delete` message-tool actions, gated by the existing `events` action gate, with typed PATCH/DELETE REST helpers, partial-PATCH runtime that only sends fields the agent provided, CLI subcommands, docs, changelog, and tests - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no new core seam, no changes to other channels, no changes to `event-list` / `event-create`, no fetch-then-merge round trip (Discord PATCH already only changes fields present in the body) ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [x] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #66791 - Related #60883 (prior `event-create` cover-image work that this builds on) - [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: agents could not update or delete Discord scheduled events through the message tool; only `event-list` and `event-create` were exposed - Real environment tested: local OpenClaw built from this branch (`pnpm install && pnpm build`) against a real Discord guild I admin, using a bot installed with `Manage Events`; plus the typed REST fake suite for the wire-shape proof - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. `pnpm openclaw message event create --guild-id --event-name "Listening Party" --start-time 2026-05-15T19:00:00Z --end-time 2026-05-15T21:00:00Z --event-type external --location "https://meet.example.com/listen" --desc "first session"` -> noted the returned event id 2. `pnpm openclaw message event edit --guild-id --event-id --desc "now featuring Album X"` -> only the description field was sent in the PATCH 3. Opened the event in Discord to confirm only the description changed; title, start/end time, and location were unchanged 4. `pnpm openclaw message event delete --guild-id --event-id ` 5. `pnpm openclaw message event list --guild-id ` to confirm the event is gone 6. Targeted Vitest suites: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/internal/api.test.ts`, `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/actions/handle-action.test.ts`, `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts`, `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/message-action-spec.test.ts`, `pnpm test src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts`, `pnpm test src/agents/tool-display.test.ts` 7. `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` (regenerated codex prompt-snapshot fixtures for the new `eventId` schema field) 8. `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck + lint + import-cycles + boundary guards) - Evidence after fix: live Discord guild walked through create -> partial-edit -> delete cleanly (screenshot attached); targeted suites all green (8 + 53 + 12 + 21 + 24 + 43 + 21 tests); `pnpm check:changed` reports `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` for all three oxlint shards and a green typecheck across all tsgo lanes - Observed result after fix: in Discord, the edit step changed only the description and left every other field byte-for-byte unchanged; the delete step removed the event from the guild's scheduled-events list. At the wire level, `event-edit` sends a partial PATCH with only the fields the agent provided and `event-delete` issues `DELETE /guilds/{guild.id}/scheduled-events/{event.id}`, both under the existing `events` action gate - What was not tested: stage / voice entity-type variants (only the `external` variant was exercised end-to-end on a real guild; the stage/voice mapping is covered by the new runtime tests) - Before evidence (optional): on `main`, `gh search code 'event-edit OR event-delete'` returns no hits in the Discord plugin or message-action surfaces ## Root Cause (if applicable) N/A (feature addition, not a regression) ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) N/A (new feature; coverage added in the PR is the smallest reliable guardrail) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [x] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: `extensions/discord/src/internal/api.test.ts` (REST shape), `extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.test.ts` (eventEdit/eventDelete partial-PATCH and gating), `extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts` (events-gate exposes the full lifecycle) - Scenario the test should lock in: PATCH/DELETE route shape, partial-field forwarding, `entity_metadata.location` encoding when `eventType` is external, `events` gate enforcement - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: covers each of the action layers (REST helper, runtime, discovery) at the seam an agent would actually exercise, without paying for a live Discord round trip - Existing test that already covers this: none for edit/delete; `event-create` had no analogous handle-action/runtime test before this PR either - If no new test is added, why not: n/a, tests added ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - New message-tool actions on Discord: `event-edit` (required `guildId`+`eventId`, optional `eventName`/`desc`/`location`/`startTime`/`endTime`/`eventType`/`channelId`/`image`) and `event-delete` (required `guildId`+`eventId`) - New CLI subcommands: `pnpm openclaw message event edit ...` and `pnpm openclaw message event delete ...` - Both actions stay behind the existing `channels.discord.actions.events` gate, so existing deployments that disable that gate stay unchanged ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: event-list / event-create -> Discord (GET / POST scheduled-events) [no edit / delete path; metadata goes stale until a human fixes it] After: event-list -> GET /guilds/{g}/scheduled-events event-create -> POST /guilds/{g}/scheduled-events event-edit -> PATCH /guilds/{g}/scheduled-events/{e} (only fields the agent provided) event-delete -> DELETE /guilds/{g}/scheduled-events/{e} ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No (rides the existing `events` action gate) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? Yes; two new outbound calls to Discord's existing `guild scheduled-events` endpoint (PATCH and DELETE), reusing the same authenticated `RequestClient` already used by `event-list` / `event-create` - Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes; two new message-tool actions added to the `events` gate - Data access scope changed? No - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: deletion is destructive, so it stays gated by the same `events` flag that already controls create; partial-PATCH avoids accidentally clearing fields the agent did not mention ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: Linux (WSL2) - Runtime/container: Node 22 + pnpm; locally built from this branch and run against a real Discord guild I admin (also covered at the wire level by the typed Discord REST fake suite) - Model/provider: n/a (action-surface change) - Integration/channel: Discord (`channels.discord`); bot installed in the test guild with the `Manage Events` permission - Relevant config (redacted): account with `channels.discord.actions.events: true` ### Steps 1. Configure a Discord account with the `events` gate enabled 2. `pnpm openclaw message event create --guild-id --event-name "Listening Party" --start-time ` and note the returned event id 3. `pnpm openclaw message event edit --guild-id --event-id --desc "now featuring Album X"` 4. `pnpm openclaw message event delete --guild-id --event-id ` ### Expected - After step 3 only the description changes; cover image, status, recurrence, and other fields stay untouched - After step 4 the event is gone from `pnpm openclaw message event list --guild-id ` ### Actual - Live Discord guild: `event create` produced a scheduled event with the listed metadata; `event edit --desc "now featuring Album X"` updated only the description in the Discord UI and left every other field unchanged; `event delete` removed the event and the follow-up `event list` returned an empty array. Screenshot of the Discord event card before and after the edit (and after the delete) attached to the PR - Wire level: partial PATCH body matches exactly the fields the agent passed (covered by `runtime.test.ts`); DELETE issues against `Routes.guildScheduledEvent("g1", "e1")` (covered by `internal/api.test.ts`) ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after (channel-actions discovery test now asserts the full lifecycle; api.test.ts now asserts PATCH/DELETE shapes) - [x] Trace/log snippets (test command output above) - [x] Screenshot/recording (Discord event card after `event create`, after `event edit --desc`, and the empty `event list` after `event delete`) - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)
Event created
Event deleted
## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: live Discord guild walkthrough of `event create` -> `event edit --desc` -> `event delete` -> `event list`, confirming via the Discord UI that the partial edit changed only the description and the delete removed the event; targeted Vitest suites listed above; `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck + lint + import-cycles + boundary); `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all 18 touched files - Edge cases checked: events gate disabled (rejects with `Discord events are disabled`); `eventType: "external"` with `location` encodes `entity_metadata.location`; omitted fields are not sent in the PATCH body; `eventDelete` returns `{ ok: true, eventId }` - What I did not verify on a live guild: `eventType: "stage"` and `eventType: "voice"` variants (only the `external` variant was exercised end-to-end; the other two are covered by the new runtime tests) ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes - Config/env changes? No (uses existing `channels.discord.actions.events` gate) - Migration needed? No ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: agent passes `eventType` change without the dependent fields Discord requires (e.g. switching to `external` without `location` or `endTime`) - Mitigation: Discord's PATCH endpoint already enforces entity-type-specific constraints server-side; the runtime forwards the error to the agent; documented in `docs/channels/discord.md` - Risk: `event-delete` is destructive - Mitigation: rides the same `events` action gate as `event-create`, so anyone who already restricted event creation continues to restrict deletion ## AI assistance This PR was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent (Claude). The diff was authored against the existing `event-create` plumbing, every change was locally typechecked, linted, formatted, and covered by Vitest, and prompt snapshot fixtures were regenerated through `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Functionality was tested manually by me (human 🤡). ## Test plan - `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/internal/api.test.ts` - `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.test.ts` - `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/actions/handle-action.test.ts` - `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts` - `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/message-action-spec.test.ts` - `pnpm test src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts` - `pnpm test src/agents/tool-display.test.ts` - `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` - `pnpm check:changed` - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ` ## Before / After Before: the Discord message tool exposed `event-list` and `event-create` only. Once an event was live, agents could not update its description, location, time window, cover image, or entity-type metadata, and could not delete the event. The CLI mirrored that gap with only `message event list` and `message event create` subcommands. After: agents can call `event-edit` (partial PATCH; only the fields the agent provides are sent, so unrelated state stays untouched) and `event-delete` through the message tool, and the CLI exposes `message event edit` / `message event delete` subcommands. Both new actions sit behind the existing `events` action gate. Discord's `PATCH` endpoint keeps enforcing entity-type-specific constraints server-side, so the runtime does not need a fetch-then-merge round trip.

target.title: feat(providers): add LongCat API support
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LongCat-2.0 is available through LongCat's hosted OpenAI-compatible API, but OpenClaw users currently need to hand-author a custom provider block. That skips native onboarding, secret discovery, catalog metadata, reasoning replay compatibility, and standard provider documentation.

Fixes #100485.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a bundled `longcat` provider plugin with `LONGCAT_API_KEY` onboarding, a static `LongCat-2.0` catalog, and the hosted `https://api.longcat.chat/openai` endpoint. The implementation reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible transport while declaring LongCat's binary `thinking` payload, `reasoning_content` replay requirement, 1M context, 128K output limit, and published pricing.

A small shared compatibility fix makes manifest-declared `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` survive catalog normalization and prevents DeepSeek-format providers from sending `reasoning_effort` when `supportsReasoningEffort` is false.

The hosted provider remains separate from self-hosted weights: local LongCat-2.0 deployments should use the existing vLLM or SGLang providers instead of adding a second LongCat runtime path.

## User Impact

Users can run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice longcat-api-key`, select `longcat/LongCat-2.0`, and use LongCat reasoning/tool-call sessions without manual provider JSON.

The live generation test is key-gated with `LONGCAT_API_KEY`. It is intentionally pending until a maintainer supplies a live API key; deterministic catalog, onboarding, payload, replay, lint, type, build, and transport proof are included now.

## Evidence

- Official contract checked against LongCat API docs, OpenClaw guide, pricing page, and the LongCat-2.0 Hugging Face model card.
- Live unauthenticated model discovery: `GET /openai/v1/models` returned `LongCat-2.0`.
- Live auth boundary: invalid-key `POST /openai/v1/chat/completions` returned HTTP 401 with `invalid_api_key`.

target.title: fix(ollama): fall back when native streams end early
target.body:
Closes #100460.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a native Ollama chat stream ending before its final response could dead-end a configured model fallback chain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama plugin now classifies only its exact incomplete-stream error as `server_error` for both local Ollama and Ollama Cloud. The stream producer and provider classifier share one constant, so this vendor-specific rule stays in the provider boundary and unrelated Ollama errors remain unclassified.

## User Impact

Users with model fallbacks configured can advance to the next candidate when Ollama closes an incomplete native stream instead of receiving a terminal request failure.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `cb6b626c1537697fa97a18c472c76632b58574a1`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/index.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` - 2 files, 163 tests passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

- Fresh branch AutoReview reported no actionable findings and rated the patch correct with 0.86 confidence.
- The maintainer-authored changelog note accurately describes the fallback behavior and credits @TurboTheTurtle.
- Upstream `ollama/ollama@964ea42` defines `ChatResponse.Done` as the completion signal and emits it from the chat completion response, confirming EOF before that response is incomplete.
- Proof gap: validation did not force a live Ollama daemon to truncate mid-stream; the producer error and provider classification are covered directly.

target.title: fix(delivery): fall back to deliveryContext.to / origin.to when session lastTo is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deliveryContextFromSession` (src/utils/delivery-context.shared.ts) rebuilds a
delivery context from a persisted session entry. It already applies a fallback
chain for the thread id:

```ts
lastThreadId: entry.lastThreadId ?? entry.deliveryContext?.threadId ?? entry.origin?.threadId,
```

but the delivery **target** gets no such chain:

```ts
lastTo: entry.lastTo,
```

If a session entry was created or migrated without `lastTo` populated — while
`entry.deliveryContext.to` and/or `entry.origin.to` are present and correct —
the derived context can resolve with **no `to` target**. Downstream, the final
reply is then silently dropped: the agent run completes normally (the user sees
"typing"), but nothing is delivered. There is no error surfaced; the only trace
is a session entry whose reply never arrives.

`normalizeSessionDeliveryFields` does merge `deliveryContext.to` in the
happy path, but the merge drops it whenever the legacy channel and the
delivery-context channel conflict (`mergeDeliveryContext` refuses to mix
targets across channels), and `origin.to` is never consulted for the target at
all — it is only read for `provider`, `accountId`, and `threadId`.

We hit this in production on a WhatsApp deployment (openclaw 2026.5.28, still
reproducible on 2026.6.11): session entries rebuilt without `lastTo` caused
every final reply on those sessions to vanish until the field was manually
backfilled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the `lastThreadId` fallback chain for `lastTo`:

```diff
--- a/src/utils/delivery-context.shared.ts
+++ b/src/utils/delivery-context.shared.ts
@@ export function deliveryContextFromSession(
   const source: DeliveryContextSessionSource = {
     route: entry.route,
     channel: entry.channel ?? entry.origin?.provider,
     lastChannel: entry.lastChannel,
-    lastTo: entry.lastTo,
+    lastTo: entry.lastTo ?? entry.deliveryContext?.to ?? entry.origin?.to,
     lastAccountId: entry.lastAccountId ?? entry.origin?.accountId,
     lastThreadId: entry.lastThreadId ?? entry.deliveryContext?.threadId ?? entry.origin?.threadId,
     origin: entry.origin,
     deliveryContext: entry.deliveryContext,
   };
```

`DeliveryContextSessionSource.origin` (src/utils/delivery-context.types.ts)
currently types only `provider` / `accountId` / `threadId`, so the type needs
the target field session entries already carry at runtime:

```diff
--- a/src/utils/delivery-context.types.ts
+++ b/src/utils/delivery-context.types.ts
@@ export type DeliveryContextSessionSource = {
   /** Older origin fields emitted before delivery context became canonical. */
   origin?: {
     provider?: string;
+    to?: string;
     accountId?: string;
     threadId?: string | number;
   };
```

Core already uses exactly this fallback chain for the same data when seeding
the reply context — src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts (current main,
~line 321):

```ts
setIfMissing(
  "OriginatingTo",
  normalizeOptionalString(
    sessionEntry.lastTo ?? sessionEntry.deliveryContext?.to ?? sessionEntry.origin?.to,
  ),
);
```

This PR makes `deliveryContextFromSession` consistent with that, and with its
own `lastThreadId` handling two lines below. No imports change; behavior is
unchanged for any entry that has `lastTo` set.

## User Impact

Sessions whose persisted entry lacks `lastTo` (but still carries the target in
`deliveryContext.to` or `origin.to`) get their final replies delivered again
instead of silently dropped. Entries that already have `lastTo` set are
completely unaffected — precedence is unchanged.

## Evidence

Added cases to `src/utils/delivery-context.test.ts` (which already covers
`deliveryContextFromSession`):

1. entry with `lastTo` undefined but `deliveryContext: { channel: "whatsapp", to: "+1555" }`
   → derived context has `to: "+1555"` (today: can resolve without a target
   when channels conflict with the legacy channel field).
2. entry with `lastTo` and `deliveryContext.to` both undefined but
   `origin: { provider: "whatsapp", to: "+1555" }` → derived context has
   `to: "+1555"` (today: `to` is undefined).
3. entry with `lastTo` set → unchanged precedence (`lastTo` wins over both).

Ran locally: `pnpm vitest run src/utils/delivery-context.test.ts` — 12/12 pass
with the fix; the new cases 1 and 2 fail without it (verified by stashing the
src change and re-running). Full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` was
not run locally (2-vCPU box); relying on CI for the wider lanes.

AI-assisted: prepared with Claude Code; the diff, tests, and this description
were human-reviewed before filing.

## Related

- #69010 (open) — stale-deliveryContext precedence for gateway agent sends;
  different direction (current route winning over persisted context), does not
  touch `deliveryContextFromSession`'s missing-target case.
- #95021 (closed) — heartbeat-mode `lastTo` inheritance across channel
  mismatches; fixed a different call path.

target.title: fix(anthropic): keep OAuth callback on loopback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic OAuth allowed the local callback listener host to be configured without validating that it was loopback-only. The earlier PR revision also derived the OAuth `redirect_uri` from that bind host, but Anthropic's current client contract requires `http://localhost:53692/callback` even when the listener binds an equivalent loopback address.

Fixes #96485.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callback bind address and provider redirect identity are separate contracts:

- `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST` is validated only when login starts and accepts `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`;
- the listener defaults to `127.0.0.1` and may bind any accepted loopback address;
- authorization URLs, manual-code prompts, and token exchange always use Anthropic's required `http://localhost:53692/callback`.

This is smaller and safer than deriving the redirect URI from local bind configuration. Direct inspection of the installed Claude Code 2.1.201 client confirmed the same contract: localhost redirect URI, loopback listener. Anthropic's public Claude Code issue #11469 documents the localhost callback behavior as well.

## User Impact

Invalid/non-loopback callback hosts fail only when Anthropic login starts, so unrelated CLI imports and commands remain unaffected. Operators can still choose IPv4 or IPv6 loopback binding without changing the provider-visible redirect URI.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwt6qx4r4ptdbg4ps3yhnj55`: `src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts`, 11/11 passed.
- The focused suite opens a real TCP callback listener on `127.0.0.1:53692`, sends an HTTP callback, and verifies both authorization and token-exchange requests use the fixed localhost redirect URI.
- Remote `oxfmt --check` passed for source and tests.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview: no actionable findings, confidence 0.96.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Live Anthropic token exchange was not run because it requires an interactive user credential. No docs change is needed; the Unreleased changelog entry is included.

target.title: fix(googlechat): fall back to text link on media upload 403
target.body:
Fixes #89430

## Summary

When Google Chat is configured with app authentication (`chat.bot` scope), any agent reply with media fails because `attachments:upload` returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Per Google's docs, media upload requires user auth (`chat.messages.create`), not app auth. The entire message is lost because the upload error propagates uncaught.

This fix catches 403 errors from the upload call in both delivery paths:
- `channel.adapters.ts` (main outbound adapter)
- `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` (sub-agent announce and monitor replies)

On 403, instead of failing the entire message, the code falls back to sending the media URL as a text link so the user still receives the artifact. Non-403 upload errors propagate unchanged.

4 regression tests cover the fallback and error propagation in both paths.

Closes #89430

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Google Chat agents with app auth cannot deliver images/files; the upload returns 403 and the entire message is lost.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v22.19.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-89606`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/wt-89606
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm build

  # Verify the fallback is in the production bundle
  grep -n '403' dist/googlechat-*.js

  # Run the regression tests
  npx vitest run extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  Terminal confirms all 4 new tests exercise the 403 fallback and error propagation:

  ```console
  $ npx vitest run extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ✓ googlechatPlugin outbound sendMedia > falls back to sending the media URL as text when upload returns 403
  ✓ googlechatPlugin outbound sendMedia > propagates non-403 upload errors
  ✓ Google Chat reply delivery > falls back to sending the media URL as text when upload returns 403
  ✓ Google Chat reply delivery > propagates non-403 upload errors to the error handler
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  24 passed (24)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** When the Google Chat attachment upload fails with 403 (app-auth scope insufficient), the adapter sends `caption + URL` as a text message instead of failing silently. The user receives the media artifact as a clickable link. Non-403 errors still propagate to the outer error handler.
- **What was not tested:** Live Google Chat workspace with a service-account-only bot, triggering a media reply to confirm the text-link fallback renders correctly in the Chat client.

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** File-source SecretRef in `messages.tts.personas.<id>.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey` is not resolved at runtime, causing `elevenlabs: not configured`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v22.19.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-89607`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/wt-89607
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm build

  # Verify the persona-level collector is in the production bundle
  cat dist/runtime-config-collectors-tts-BgBmCuWf.js

  # Run the regression tests
  npx vitest run src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  The persona-level iteration is active in the production bundle:

  ```console
  $ cat dist/runtime-config-collectors-tts-BgBmCuWf.js
  ...
  const personas = params.tts.personas;
  if (isRecord(personas)) for (const [personaId, persona] of Object.entries(personas)) {
  if (!isRecord(persona)) continue;
  const personaProviders = persona.providers;
  if (!isRecord(personaProviders)) continue;
  for (const [providerId, providerConfig] of Object.entries(personaProviders)) {
  if (!isRecord(providerConfig)) continue;
  collectProviderApiKeyAssignment({
  providerId,
  providerConfig,
  pathPrefix: `${params.pathPrefix}.personas.${personaId}`,
  ...
  ```

  Terminal confirms all 5 new tests exercise the persona SecretRef collection:

  ```console
  $ npx vitest run src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from top-level TTS providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from persona-level TTS provider overrides
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from both top-level and persona-level providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > skips personas without providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects persona refs with agent-level path prefix
  Test Files  1 passed (1)

target.title: feat(atomicchat): add Atomic Chat as a bundled local provider
target.body:
Closes #89617

## What & why

[Atomic Chat](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/Atomic-Chat) is an open-source cross-platform desktop/mobile app that runs open-weight LLMs locally and exposes a single **OpenAI-compatible** HTTP API at `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1` (a Rust proxy fronting a llama.cpp/TurboQuant fork and MLX-VLM). It's the same shape as the local providers OpenClaw already bundles (LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang).

This adds a bundled, `enabledByDefault: true` provider plugin so Atomic Chat shows up **natively** in the provider list and onboarding, instead of requiring a hand-written custom provider. It mirrors the `sglang` plugin: an OpenAI-compatible self-hosted provider with model auto-discovery from `/v1/models`.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider id | `atomicchat` |
| API | `openai-completions` |
| Default base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1` |
| Auth env var | `ATOMIC_CHAT_API_KEY` (any non-empty value; loopback is unauthenticated by default) |
| Pricing | `external: false` (local) |

## Changes

- **`extensions/atomicchat/`** — new bundled provider plugin (defaults, models, index, manifest, README, unit test). Uses the shared `openai-completions` self-hosted setup/discovery helpers, exactly like `sglang`.
- **`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts`** — register `atomicchat` in `BUILT_IN_MODEL_PROVIDER_OVERLAY_IDS`.
- **`src/commands/models/list.provider-catalog.ts`** — add `atomicchat` to `SELF_HOSTED_DISCOVERY_PROVIDER_IDS`.
- **Docs** — new `docs/providers/atomicchat.md`, entry in the provider directory, a row in `docs/gateway/local-models.md`, a nav entry in `docs/docs.json`, and regenerated `docs/plugins/*` (added `atomicchat` → `Atomic Chat` to the inventory humanize map).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Before this change OpenClaw had no first-class Atomic Chat provider — users had to hand-write a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. After the change, `atomicchat` is a bundled provider that appears natively in the picker/onboarding and auto-discovers models from the running Atomic Chat server.

**Real environment tested:** macOS (Apple Silicon). Atomic Chat desktop app running its OpenAI-compatible server on `127.0.0.1:1337`, serving `unsloth/Qwen3_5-9B-GGUF-Qwen3_5-9B-IQ4_XS`. OpenClaw built and run from this branch via `node scripts/run-node.mjs`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
1. `node scripts/run-node.mjs models list --provider atomicchat` (with `ATOMIC_CHAT_API_KEY` set)
2. `node scripts/run-node.mjs infer model run --local --model atomicchat/unsloth/Qwen3_5-9B-GGUF-Qwen3_5-9B-IQ4_XS --prompt "yo" --json`
3. `node scripts/run-node.mjs onboard` and selected the provider in the picker

**Evidence after fix:**

Provider recognized and model auto-discovered from `/v1/models`:

```
Model                                      Input   Ctx    Local Auth
atomicchat/unsloth/Qwen3_5-9B-GGUF-Qwen... text    125k   yes   yes
```

End-to-end local inference through the provider:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "atomicchat",
  "model": "unsloth/Qwen3_5-9B-GGUF-Qwen3_5-9B-IQ4_XS",
  "outputs": [{ "text": "Yo! What's up? How can I help you today?", "mediaUrl": null }]
}
```

Onboarding picker lists it as **Atomic Chat (Local AI provider)** and pre-fills `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1`.

Supplemental automated tests: `pnpm test:extension atomicchat` → 3 passed; `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` → 935 passed.

**Observed result after fix:** Atomic Chat is selectable natively, auto-discovers its model, and a local `yo` turn routes through the `atomicchat` provider and returns a real model reply (`transport: "local"`, `provider: "atomicchat"`).

**What was not tested:** Vision/image input (registered as text; image models can be enabled with `input: ["text","image"]`). Windows/Linux hosts (validated on macOS Apple Silicon only).

---

Maintainer edits are enabled on this fork branch. Happy to maintain the plugin.

> Note: the `dependency-guard` check flags the new `extensions/atomicchat/package.json` because adding any workspace package counts as a dependency-graph change. That requires an admin / `@openclaw/openclaw-secops` `/allow-dependencies-change` on this head SHA — there are no third-party runtime dependencies added.
